title: Cycle Codes and Decoded Quantum Interferometry
authors: Anuj Apte, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Andi Gu, Stephen P. Jordan, Ojas Parekh, Ruslan Shaydulin, Jacob Watkins, Noureldin Yosri, Adam Zalcman
abstract: Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) reduces optimization problems with two-variable constraints to decoding cycle codes. For one such problem, namely MaxCut, prior work showed that DQI achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee only on linear-girth graphs, for which MaxCut is classically easy. However, these no-go results rely on minimum distance assumptions that do not represent true decodability thresholds for common noise channels, thus underestimating actual DQI performance. To estimate the true performance, we derive DQI satisfaction guarantees in the presence of imperfect decoding for fixed instances and generalize prior results for random instances. We then study homological cycle codes over arbitrary finite fields, and show that minimum-weight decoding is NP-hard for every field of size $q>2$, in contrast with known results for binary cycle codes. On the Linial--Simkin ensemble of regular graphs with logarithmic girth, we prove maximum-likelihood recovery bounds and a strong converse for a family of non-uniform additive noise channels. Moreover, LP decoders provide polynomial-time recovery of a positive fraction of randomly located errors with arbitrary values. These results allow us to prove upper and lower bounds on the approximate optima achievable by DQI when restricted to classical decoders. These bounds rule out quantum advantage in the regimes we analyze but also identify a family of regular Max-$k$-Cut instances on which DQI efficiently achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee.
summary: This work analyzes Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) applied to optimization problems modeled by cycle codes. The authors derive rigorous bounds on DQI's achievable performance by studying decoding guarantees for these codes over finite fields. The results constrain the potential quantum advantage by establishing performance limits based on classical decoding capabilities.
main_problem: The paper investigates the performance limits of Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) when applied to solving optimization problems constrained by cycle codes.
main_result: The analysis establishes upper and lower bounds on the approximate optima achievable by DQI using classical decoders, ruling out quantum advantage in the analyzed regimes but identifying specific instances where a nontrivial guarantee exists.
method: The authors derive satisfaction guarantees by analyzing the decoding process for homological cycle codes over finite fields, employing techniques like Linear Programming (LP) formulations and bounding interference terms.
model_or_system: The model centers on cycle codes, which reduce optimization problems like MaxCut to decoding problems. The analysis is performed over arbitrary finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$ and utilizes the Linial–Simkin ensemble of regular graphs.
key_observables: Satisfaction fraction guarantee, reliability threshold ($\delta_{\text{rel}}$), and the minimum-weight decoding complexity.
important_parameters: Field size $q$, graph degree $D$, error probability $p$, and the girth of the underlying graph.
main_assumptions: The initial 'no-go' results relied on minimum distance assumptions that underestimate true DQI performance; the analysis also assumes deterministic syndrome-consistent mappings.
figures_summary: The notes mention Table 1 comparing binary vs. non-binary cycle codes, and Table 2 comparing algorithmic performance metrics for different decoding techniques.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the problem context (DQI and cycle codes), then deriving general satisfaction guarantees under imperfect decoding, followed by detailed analysis of ML decoding bounds using Fourier transforms, and concluding with LP formulations and trellis constructions to prove recovery guarantees.
why_interesting: While the core topic is coding theory applied to optimization, the rigorous analysis of error thresholds and recovery bounds using advanced mathematical tools (LP, random walks) is highly relevant to understanding the limits of quantum error correction and quantum computation feasibility.

figures.caption: Figure 1: LP word-error rates on Linial–Simkin graphs with c = 0.9 and m = Dn/2 symbols. Each curve uses eight graphs. For q = 2, 3, 5, respectively, the sample counts per noise level are 64, 64, 64 at n = 1024; 64, 64, 32 at n = 4096; 32, 32, 16 at n = 16384; and 16, 8, 8 at n = 65536. The dashed lines mark the ML cycle upper bound (78); the dotted lines mark the certified LP rate (85). Open symbols distinguish complete fresh-object solves from the standard runs. Vertical intervals span the possible full-sample word-error rates when some solves time out; they are not statistical error bars. Curves are not continued through such points.

The table lists all four paths from the required start to the required end. Dashed nodes and edges are included in the full construction but lie on no such path; they carry zero flow in the LP.
